To forecast the progress of the Millennium Prize Problems (MPPs), I am estimating the combined capability progression of AI systems and humans (“AI-Humans”) to both solve MPPs (“AI Capability Progression”) and work together on collaborative applications (“AI Collaborative Progression”).

AI Capability Progression:
To determine AI Capability Progression, I am primarily estimating the applicability of AI systems to general problem solving. Specifically, I am estimating their ability to help d
-devolve chosen general problems into specialized problems, find analogous problems to use as solutions, make exact (or as close as reasonable) judgments about provable properties, and otherwise perform a diverse variety of problem solving strategies. (Note that I am assuming progress on the exact particular problem-solving strategies is relatively unimportant. That is to say, while progress on these specific problem solving strategies would be relevant and worth monitoring, I am further expecting progress on more general problem solving strategies to be more important than progress on any one specific strategy. This is a very simple, first-order assumption.)
While the mode of the distribution of AI infrastructure cost over time is uncertain, I am assuming that it will go down. Specifically, if I am focusing only on financial cost (externalities, energy consumption, etc.), I assume the required infrastructure capital for AI progress at any given time is no more than a modest multiple of the current global GDP, unless societal collapse occurs. If societal collapse occurs, the relevant cost can be scaled by the societal collapse fraction to MPP solving capability set during that period. Shifts are thus caused by differences in short-term money flows, which exist but are likely minor over the given time scales. Thus, I am primarily considering the distribution of headway from AI computer power enablement acting on karma.
(Note that I am implicitly assuming there will likely not be prompt AI moral progress to the degree that this would significantly change the valuation of developing MPPs. While the importance of such progress should be considered, and I believe it will be modest compared to the scale of potential MPP progress, I am still motivated by my existing Metaphysical Assumptions.)
In terms of AI Collaborative Progression, I am estimating the same for AI-Humans. I expect people to adopt increasingly productive hybrids of human and AI ability in their everyday work, incrementally enhancing their ability to do such work. As AI systems become more collaborative and fit into the human workflow, I expect incremental progress to be achieved more quickly via normal human-AI symbiosis, despite societal factors like hard labor not decreasing IPs by default.
Explaining the Inflection Point at 2040-2050:
Based on my research, I assume that the progress of AI and human collaborations in solving the millennium prize problems (MPPs) will gradually gain headway at an initially slow pace through various collaborations, and exponentially increase by 2050. Therefore, my forecast's probability slope shifts from 0 to high values at this point. This accelerating trend is likely due to the increasing capability of AIs and humans to work together more effectively, combined with both sustained societal factors and increasingly s-small reaching skill gain in such collaborations, affording much of useful headway via AI-Human collaboration. Additionally, I assume that the diminishing returns in human-AI symbiotic collaboration will become noticeable well before 2050. As a result, I forecast that by 2050, useful headway will be primarily gained via AI-Human collaboration. My probabilities remain high at this point to reflect the continuous decrease in societal barriers, technological headway increases, and other factors. There may still be some small headway gained via normal human-AI collaboration, but its relatively continuous elimination and therefore lessening of advance headway via such progressions are counteracted by the increase in societal barriers, technological headway, and other factors. As a result, I forecast modestly higher probabilities for 2050 than for previous time periods.
formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
